mechanism: Bill Williams Alligator: three SMMA on median price—Jaw(13,shift8), Teeth(8,shift5), Lips(5,shift3). Lines spreading apart = trending regime; converging = consolidation. Buy path further requires close breaking Jaw bottom→top after Fractal Down; sell is the mirror.
data_needed: iAlligator(13,8,8,5,5,3,MODE_SMMA,PRICE_MEDIAN) jaws/teeth/lips buffers; close prices; optional fractal direction.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: MT5 chart _Symbol/_Period (generic FX); Strategy Tester optimization on fractal/Alligator thresholds across sessions.
why_new_for_mis: Three-line lag stack as an explicit trend-vs-chop regime sensor—MIS can read Jaw–Lips separation / ordering as a continuous consolidation score rather than a binary MA slope.
quote: When the lines start to spread apart, it signals a trend; when they converge, it suggests the market is in a phase of consolidation.

mechanism: Awesome Oscillator = SMA(median,5)−SMA(median,34) histogram; Accelerator Oscillator is AO’s acceleration, color-coded green(up)/red(down) around zero. Entry fires when AO crosses zero in the trade direction and AC color confirms (green for buy, red for sell); exits on opposite AO zero-cross.
data_needed: iAO and iAC buffers; AC color buffer index; prior two AO bars for cross detect.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: _Symbol/_Period; histogram subwindows; bar-close evaluation via isNewBar.
why_new_for_mis: Paired momentum-level (AO zero) plus acceleration-color (AC) change sensor—detects regime flips before full trend mature, usable as a lightweight momentum-state machine.
quote: The AC oscillates around a zero line, moving in green (positive) or red (negative) zones… used in conjunction with the AO indicator to provide confirmation of market strength and momentum shifts.

mechanism: Classic Williams fractal: five consecutive bars with middle bar highest (Fractal Up) or lowest (Fractal Down). EA tracks lastFractal_value/direction (UP/DOWN/NEUTRAL) from iFractals buffers shifted ≥2 bars so the pattern is confirmed; Fractal Down primes buys, Fractal Up primes sells.
data_needed: iFractals up/down buffers; last fractal value and direction state.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: _Symbol/_Period; fractals form ≥3 bars back from current.
why_new_for_mis: Discrete local-extremum change events as a structural sensor—MIS can stream confirmed swing tags without relying on continuous oscillators.
quote: The fractals are formed when there are five consecutive bars with the middle bar being the highest or lowest. They signal the potential start of a new trend or a price reversal.

mechanism: Ichimoku Senkou Span A/B (params 8,29,34) form the Kumo. isKumo_Above = SpanA>SpanB (bullish cloud), isKumo_Below = SpanA<SpanB. Buy when AO crosses above zero AND cloud is bearish AND close > both spans (breakout through cloud); sell is the mirror. Exits on opposite AO zero-cross. Notes choppy false signals inside cloud during consolidation.
data_needed: iIchimoku(8,29,34) SENKOUSPANA/B lines; iAO; prior close.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: _Symbol/_Period; new-bar gated; trailing stop 3000 points in tester.
why_new_for_mis: Cloud polarity plus price-vs-both-spans breakout as a dynamic S/R regime sensor—richer than a single MA cross because the cloud encodes forward-shifted support/resistance state.
quote: When the price breaks out above the Kumo, it signals a potential bullish trend, while a breakout below indicates a possible bearish trend.

mechanism: RSI(14,PRICE_CLOSE) on PERIOD_CURRENT: buy when prior RSI>30 and current RSI≤30 (cross into oversold); sell when prior RSI<70 and current≥70 (cross into overbought). Once fired, ZoneRecovery class manages adverse moves via zone/target levels and lot multiplier—sensing layer is the RSI threshold cross only.
data_needed: iRSI handle; 2-bar RSI buffer; lastBarTime gate.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: _Symbol with PERIOD_CURRENT; year-2024 tester run; zonePts/targetPts in points.
why_new_for_mis: Classic OB/OS cross as a discrete regime-edge event for mean-reversion baskets—MIS can reuse the same 30/70 edge detector independently of the recovery money-management wrapper.
quote: Trade entries are triggered when the RSI crosses key thresholds—typically 30 for oversold (buy) and 70 for overbought (sell) conditions.

mechanism: Same RSI 30/70 crosses as Part 3, but each signal spawns an independent PositionRecovery basket in recoveryArray[] with its own zoneHigh/Low, targets, tickets, and trailing state. Baskets managed in a loop without interfering—sensing is still RSI, architecture isolates concurrent regime events.
data_needed: rsiBuffer; recoveryArray of PositionRecovery; per-basket zone/ticket state.
why_new_for_mis: Concurrent multi-instance handling of identical regime signals—MIS pattern for tracking several independent regime episodes on one symbol without collapsing state.
quote: Each trading signal generated by the RSI indicator will correspond to its unique basket, stored as an element within an array.

mechanism: Fast MA(14) vs Slow MA(50) crossover on new bar: buy when fast crosses above slow and RSI≥buyThreshold (default 50); sell when fast crosses below slow and RSI≤sellThreshold. Boolean weekday inputs (Sun…Sat) gate execution via TimeToStruct day_of_week—skips historically weak sessions.
data_needed: iMA fast/slow; iRSI; MqlDateTime day_of_week; day enable flags.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: _Symbol/_Period; RSI TF selectable; 2024 yearly tester; dashboard of positions/profit.
why_new_for_mis: Combines trend-cross regime with momentum confirmation and a calendar-day regime mask—MIS can treat weekday acceptance as a first-class session-quality sensor.
quote: The strategy will also incorporate a trading day filter to optimize performance by avoiding trades on days with historically low volatility or poor performance.

mechanism: Scan last rangeCandles (default 7) from startingIndex=1: consolidation if consecutive highs and lows each differ by ≤ maxDeviation points (default 50). Then record highestHigh/lowestLow PriceIndex. Extend range while bar1 stays inside; breakout when close(1) > high or < low of range.
data_needed: high/low series; rangeCandles; maxDeviation*_Point; PriceIndex highest/lowest.
why_new_for_mis: Explicit tight-range regime sensor from pairwise high/low equality—feeds breakout/impulse pipelines and is reusable without Smart-Money labels.
quote: If both highs and lows are nearly equal, it's a consolidation range.

mechanism: After range breakout, wait waitBars (default 3) then DetectImpulsiveMovement: impulseThresholdPrice = (breakoutHigh−breakoutLow)×threshold. If close within next impulseBars ≥ high+threshold → bullish OB; ≤ low−threshold → bearish OB; else draw range only (no OB). Valid OBs stored and traded on retest pierce of OB high/low.
data_needed: impulseHigh/Low from prior range; waitBars; close(i); OB rectangle arrays.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: _Symbol/_Period; SL/TP 1500 points on OB retest trades.
why_new_for_mis: Filters weak breakouts via post-breakout displacement vs range height—MIS can gate liquidity-zone creation on impulse confirmation rather than every range escape.
quote: If the preceding three candles do not show impulsive movement, we will not validate an order block. Instead, we will only draw the consolidation range.

mechanism: MA(21) swing trigger opens initial trade; subsequent grid orders at fixed spacing double lot size; exit by currency profit target or weighted-breakeven±points. After full read: execution/risk scaffolding, not a market sensing construct.
why_new_for_mis: No new MIS sensing—grid spacing and lot doubling are position-management mechanics.
quote: The lot size is doubled with each grid order.

mechanism: PivotLeft/Right swing scan builds pivots[]; last five must be H-L-H-L-H (bearish) or L-H-L-H-L (bullish). XA=diff; B≈0.786·XA (±Tolerance); BC in [0.382,0.886]·XA; CD in [1.27,1.618]·XA with D beyond X. Lock pattern on formation bar; trade only after next-bar confirmation (anti-repaint); TP ladder toward C.
data_needed: Pivot array; Fibonacci ratio checks; g_patternFormationBar / g_lockedPatternX.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: M5 half-year tester (~65 trades); Tolerance default 10% of XA; any _Symbol.
why_new_for_mis: Geometric Fibonacci multi-leg reversal sensor with explicit anti-repaint lock—structured sequence pattern beyond single-bar oscillators.
quote: pivot B should ideally occur at approximately a 78.6% retracement of the XA move… CD should extend between 127% and 161.8% of the XA move.

mechanism: User GMT SessionStart/End (default 23:00–03:00) with overnight handling: CopyRates on BoxTimeframe (M15/M30), find max high and min low (and their bar times) inside [sessionStart,sessionEnd]. Draw box/labels; once per sessionEnd. Defines consolidation regime for the Asian window.
data_needed: Session hour/minute inputs; Bars/CopyRates on BoxTimeframe; BoxHigh/BoxLow/BoxHighTime/BoxLowTime.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: FX _Symbol; box TF M15 or M30; exit hour default 13:00 GMT; 2023 yearly tester.
why_new_for_mis: Clock-bounded session range as a first-class regime sensor—MIS can emit Asian-range height/position as overnight liquidity/compression context for later sessions.
quote: define the session box by capturing the highest high and the lowest low within a specific time window—typically between 23:00 and 03:00 Greenwich Mean Time (GMT).

mechanism: After box computed and before TradeExitTime: MA(50) vs bid → bullish/bearish. Bullish → BuyStop at BoxHigh+offset, SL below BoxLow−offset, TP via RiskToReward; bearish → SellStop mirror. At exit time close positions and delete pending stops. Optional trailing stop.
data_needed: maHandle value; BoxHigh/Low; BreakoutOffsetPips; RiskToReward; tradeExitTime.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: _Symbol; MA on chart TF; pending GTC stops; 2023 backtest.
why_new_for_mis: Session-range breakout pending orders gated by trend filter—change sensor that only arms breakouts aligned with MA regime, plus hard time-stop on the setup.
quote: place a pending buy-stop order slightly above the top of the box if market conditions confirm a bullish trend—using a moving average… for trend confirmation.

mechanism: Buy when SMMA(11,median) crosses above SMMA(25,median) AND RSI(27)>threshold(58) AND CCI(36)>0 AND CCI(55)>0; sell when fast crosses below slow AND RSI<(100−threshold) AND both CCIs<0. SL at recent pivot low/high (left/right=2); TP fixed points. Designed for higher timeframes.
data_needed: iMA SMMA median 11/25; iRSI 27; iCCI 36/55; GetPivotLow/High.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: _Symbol higher TF preferred; 2023–2024 tester; TP 300 points.
why_new_for_mis: Conjunctive dual-horizon CCI plus RSI-gated MA cross—stricter momentum-regime mask than single-oscillator confirmation.
quote: generate buy signals when a fast-moving average crosses above a slower-moving average… while confirming the signal with momentum indicators, which are an RSI and two different CCI values.

mechanism: MA close crossover opens per-signal BasketInfo with unique magic; grid adds scaled lots; breakeven TP rewrite and profit/points closure. Full read: multi-instance trade-management scaffold, not incremental market sensing beyond the MA trigger already covered in the series.
why_new_for_mis: No new MIS sensing—layered grid baskets are execution architecture.
quote: This strategy we're about to implement isn’t about predicting the market’s direction but rather about profiting from the natural flow of prices.

mechanism: Build OBs from consolidation→breakout→impulse (same family as Part 6). Mitigation event: bullish OB mitigated when close(1)<OB low → sell; bearish OB mitigated when close(1)>OB high → buy. Mark mitigated (color→gray, flag), trade once, then drop expired OBs. Optional trailing stop.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: _Symbol/_Period; consolidationBars=7; maxConsolidationSpread=50 pts; impulse wait bars; SL/TP 1500 pts.
why_new_for_mis: Failed-hold / liquidity-absorption event on institutional zones—MIS can treat OB pierce as a liquidity-regime flip distinct from simple support breaks.
quote: Mitigation occurs when a price breaks through an order block, indicating a failure in its holding structure.
